basic_info: 45-year-old male (gender confirmed) presenting with soreness, swelling, and numbness following a brick injury to the foot during yard work.
present_illness: The patient dropped a landscape brick on their foot during yard work, resulting in soreness, swelling, and numbness. The injury occurred yesterday, and the patient has noticed changes in sensation and mobility since then. The patient is unable to put weight on the foot. The pain is on the bottom and top of the foot, and there's some bruising there. The patient is unable to feel their whole foot, and the numbness does not radiate to other parts of the leg. No tingling or burning sensations reported. The numbness is all over the foot, both the top and the bottom. It's not worse in one area than another, just the whole foot feels numb. I don't remember having any nerve issues or injuries in this foot before. The patient denies any weakness or difficulty moving their toes or foot since the injury, though they report an inability to feel anything on their foot. The numbness has been pretty constant since the injury, but sometimes it feels like it gets a little worse when I move my foot or put pressure on it. It's been like that all day, really.
past_history: No prior injuries or conditions affecting the foot, including diabetes or neuropathy. History of ankle issues, including a broken ankle twenty years ago and surgery on the other ankle. No previous episodes of numbness or tingling in the foot, even if unrelated to trauma.
physical_exam: Vital signs: BP 120/80 mmHg, HR 78 bpm, Temp 36.8°C. Physical examination of the foot reveals swelling and tenderness over the midfoot region, with decreased sensation to light touch over the dorsum of the foot and toes. Bruising noted on the bottom and top of the foot. No visible deformity or bruising noted. No signs of compartment syndrome, such as pain with passive stretching or tightness of the fascia. No changes in color, temperature, or pulse noted in the affected foot. No weakness or difficulty moving toes or foot noted on examination.
aux_exam: X-ray of the foot (taken today) shows no evidence of fracture or dislocation. MRI (scheduled for tomorrow) to evaluate for soft tissue injury or nerve involvement.
